full_judgment:
5. Mr. Zakir Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the opposite party No. 1 failed to make any prayer before the Presiding Officer for recounting of the ballot papers, nor the opposite party No. 1 made any objection/prayer in the election application for recounting the votes and as such this recounting is absolutely without jurisdiction. In support of his, submission, he has referred to a decision reported in 32 DLR (AD), 186. It is now well settled that before recounting of the ballot papers of the contesting candidates, the Court must find that such recounting is absolutely necessary and without recounting, it may not be possible for the Tribunal to arrive at a correct decision to settle the dispute in question. Mr. Zakir Ahmed submits that there is no satisfaction and finding of the Tribunal as to recounting of the votes of the contesting candidates. It is difficult to accept the above contention of Mr. Zakir Ahmed in view of the fact that the order for recounting was passed on 20.10.90 and against the order the present petitioner moved a Revisional application before this Court and the same was summarily rejected vide Civil Order No. 2363 dated 28.10.90. Against that order of this Court dated 28.10.90 no further step was taken by the present petitioner. 

 8. It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that there was no prayer for recounting before the Presiding Officer or there was no specific prayer for recounting before the Election Tribunal. On filing the election 'dispute case, the entire matter became sub-jeudice before the Election Tribunal, and after perusing materials and the evidence on record, if the Tribunal feels that for settling the dispute in a matter like this it is necessary to recount the ballot papers, then there is no bar for recounting of such ballot papers. There might not be any specific prayer in the election petition, but there is a prayer for settling aside the election of the elected Chairman and also for declaring the opposite party No. 1 as duly elected Chairman of the said Union Parishad. In this view of the matter, I find no substance in the contention of Mr. Zakir Ahmed. Mr. Zakir Ahmed submits that the Courts below committed an error of a law in not consider ink the materials, evidence on record and for such non-consideration of evidence, the judgments of the lower Appellate Court as well as of the Tribunal are liable to be set aside. But, unfortunately, the learned Advocate for the petitioner fails to lay his finger on any evidence on record which was not duly considered or which was misconstrued by the Tribunal as well as the Lower Appellate Court. In this view of the matter, I find no substance in the above contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner. Mr. Alimuzzaman Chowdhury the learned Advocate for opposite party No. 1 submits that the decision reported in 38DLR (AD) 275 for all purpose supports the case of the Opposite Party No. 1. In that case, the Election Tribunal as well as the High Court Division of the Supreme Court recounted the ballot papers of the contesting candidates. After the judgment, it was challenged in Appellate Division, alleging that the High Court Division has no jurisdiction to recount the ballot papers of the contesting candidates in its writ Jurisdiction. However, the Appellate Division dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment of the High Court Division. If it is required in the interest of justice and if it is found by the Tribunal that without recounting the ballot papers of the contesting candidates the fair justice cannot be dispensed with in a particular case, I am of the view that in such a case the Tribunal is very much competent to recount the ballot papers of the contesting candidates in order to arrive at a correct decision in the case and also to do substantial justice. In view of the above, I do not find any substance in the present Revisional application and as such the Rule is discharged but there will be no order as to cost. The judgment and order of the Lower Appellate Court affirming those of the Tribunal are hereby affirmed. The order of stay passed by this court earlier is hereby vacated.
